gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each NAS costs to run 24/7 as a web server next to what hosting costs per year. Here is that comparison. At the August 2026 US average rate of 18.16¢/kWh, UGREEN's published 16.38 W for the DXP2800 works out to $26.06 a year in electricity. That is more than the whole $23.88 a year Hostinger charges for Premium WordPress hosting on its 48-month intro term. QNAP's TS-264-8G uses $46.27 a year (29.086 W), almost as much as a $4 a month DigitalOcean server ($48). Against renewal-rate shared hosting ($119.88–131.88 a year), a $389.99 DXP2800 bought only for the website pays back in about 4.2 years, before any drives.
standout_why: ChatGPT ran no search and got no results, so no rival page was there to cite. Its answer gave electricity as an unsourced '$20–60 incremental' a year and hosting as an unsourced '$60–240'. It had no wattage for any model, no electricity rate, no intro price set against renewal price, and no payback period. It also said 'assumes you already own the NAS', which leaves out anyone thinking of buying one to host a site.
decides: If you already own a 2-bay Intel NAS, it confirms the 'yes': running it costs $8–27 a year (DXP2800/DS225+, from the hibernation and access figures), about $1–2 a month. If you'd be buying one just to host a site, the answer flips. Electricity alone costs about as much as intro-rate shared hosting or a $4 VPS, and the hardware takes about 4 years to pay back even against renewal prices. The QNAP TS-264-8G draws the most power, so it costs the most to run as a web host.
